#### 1.1 Overview

This is a five-year project on rice farming in Thailand, targeting 21 provinces in the three most important rice-growing regions of the country: the north, the northeast and the east (see map). The project will be implemented by the Department of Agriculture for rice farming in Thailand. As such, it is a cross-cutting, medium-term project with a dual objective:

(a) To adapt rice farming in Thailand to order to reduce the negative impacts of observed and anticipated climate change conditions; and

(b) To reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions resulting from rice farming in order to help mitigate climate change.

Equitable access to finance is a key element of the GCF’s strategy to increase global investment flows to early-stage bio-businesses in the Amazon region in the form of direct equity, equity-like instruments and other financial products. The GCF will provide funding through its own funds under administration by the IDB (such as IDB Lab) and other co-finance. These schemes are considered effective tools to maximize the potential impact of financing operations in early-stage high-potential bio-businesses. They can be used for both equity investments and equity-like investments while offering more value for innovative companies. Equity will be used for more mature bio-businesses (i.e., those that have already demonstrated a proof-of-concept or are at an earlier viable product phase), have positive revenues, and are looking for gaining market traction.
